strings.SPS_fascism_2_party_long: Falange Española Tradicionalista y de las Juntas de Ofensiva Nacional Sindicalista
strings.SPS_heirs_18_july_desc:
In 1936, the patriotic Nationalist generals would rise against the degenerate Republican government in a bid to save Holy Spain from destruction. Carlos Iniesta Cano follows in their footsteps, stepping in against the failing government of Franco in order to save the Spanish state from falling into anarchy.

With this spirit of historical inheritance unites the people and politicians under the Junta, ordained by history to come out victorious like the one before it, unity is paramount to the vast coalition of the state. However, this unity remains dependent on one thing alone; the victories at the front.
strings.SPS_german_contacts_desc:
The Reich and Iberia have not had the best relations. This coldness however came near entirely from the Portuguese side of the peninsula, with its Spanish counterpart housing many that had supported the Nazis ever since the outbreak of the Civil War.

Thus, with the peninsula falling into anarchy, the old ally of the Nationalists would once come to their aid, with German arms fueling the war effort against the Republicans. However, with their influence growing by the day, it is far from a secret that the aid isn't free and sooner or later the Junta will need to pay back the Hun, one way or another.
strings.SPS_Tomas_Rebull_hog_desc:
President of the National Junta
Corporate Statism
--------------
The bulwark of civilisation is threatened. To arms! Veteran of the Spanish Civil War, the Eastern Front, and now the Iberian Wars, Tomás García Rebull is keenly aware of what will come should the forces of order fail. Among the original young Blueshirt combatants, the oldshirt is the premier Falangist inside the junta, striving for legislative and combative victory so that Spain may see a new spring dawn.

Lieutenant General García is also the ideal Falangist collaborator for the junta. This is because the blue general still holds a purified version of the old regime as perfect. A perfect blend of Falangism and military leadership, who stand above and beyond petty party politics. Thus, he will typically put the interests of the army first, trying to redirect National Syndicalist energy toward loyalty to the regime, and leveraging Falangist policies for his service.
strings.SPS_Jose_Codon_for_desc:
Secretary of Foreign Affairs
Absolute Monarchy
--------------
Of all Christian virtues, José María Codón embraces temperance. Despite intransigent Carlist complaints, only in tandem with the Spanish far-right was liberalism's march halted, and traditionalists afforded political posts. Thus, he preaches a rare sermon of a Falangist-Carlist fraternity forming the spine of Spain; for this, the Falangists tolerate him, assured he has not taken the ministry to stymy them.

As foreign minister, María Codón is perfectly suited and perfectly powerless. A Carlist long estranged from Carlism due to his immoderate Francoism, and an enthusiast of the junta, he represents Nationalists well. However, much to the Falangists' glee, the Carlist minister is consumed by difficulties. He must keep German aid flowing and avoid dependency, seeking wider fascist support. Due to the wars, those formerly in Iberia's orbit are ignoring his attempts to reestablish ties.
strings.SPS_Manuel_Valdes_Larranaga_eco_desc:
Coordinator of the Economic Commissions
Corporate Statism
--------------
Numbering among the Falange's founders and gunmen during the Second Republic, Manuel Valdés Larrañaga knows collaboration is not a dirty word. From the first instance, he knew that the vision of a unitary Spain lay in synthesis, not the doomed agitation of intransigents. While disloyal Falangists were eased out, the oldshirt does not feel marginalized to have been made an ambassador duty in 1950, but rewarded for his loyalty to Franco.

It is for that loyal service record that Valdés has been made minister of economy. In 1941, he was called upon to tame the corporatist Sindicato Vertical, bringing them closer to the conservative-religious consensus. Therefore, having weighed what Falangists they could abide in government, the army called upon the stout collaborator to yet again discipline the slavish Germanophilia and revolutionary national syndicalism swirling in fascist trade unionism.
strings.SPS_Alfonso_Perez_sec_desc:
Secretary of War
Fascism
--------------
Peace has been taken from Spain, from Lieutenant General Alfonso Pérez-Viñeta. First fighting in the First Spanish Civil War as a battalion commander, he sits among his colleagues in the army's high command, sharing their trajectory, sharing their view of the fiery remains of their nation, sharing in their fury. In that, he is García Rebull's man, following him into reactionary politics and a subordination of Falangist interests to the army's.

Carrying the cross of Primo de Rivera's crusade, Pérez has sworn to be remembered as the bane of all who would render Spain. As Minister of the Army, he has taken an absolutist approach, dedicating every resource he can get toward crushing the rebellions. Hungry for peace, the junta has unleashed his burning zeal upon Spain, so that the movement might impress, requisition, and divert from budget and civilian alike. War is here, with all it brings.
strings.SPS_Angel_Ramirez_Cartagena: Ángel Ramírez de Cartagena y Marcaida
strings.SPS_the_burning_peninsula_desc:
Our Spain burns in the fires of civil conflict, brother seeking to tear apart his brother as the malign tendrils of treachery infect the very lifeblood of our nation. How many towns have been leveled so far? How many patriots murdered in their beds?

No more.

Spain's salvation has come, peace will soon be at hand. Across the nation the call shall go out that, finally, Spain's most loyal children no longer fear themselves. But soon, Spain's enemies will learn to fear them, for every traitor deserves the terror of justice.
strings.SPS_the_end_of_weakness_desc:
How did we get here? How was Spain allowed to fall to such horror and despair? The legacy is written in blood, and we can read it well. Did we assert ourselves after saving the nation in the 30s? Did we confront the challenges of the post-war world proudly, as men of Spain ought to? No, we cowered. We begged the Portuguese to justify us, cared more about making councils and committees for old men to argue than doing what was necessary. Spain failed because her people were led by the weak.

But Spain need not fear, for her surgeons see her malady. Spain shall not be prostrated upon the tides of history, helpless against enemies exterior and interior. No more will she beg and weep for proper governance. There will be no more compromise. No more bickering.

No more weakness.
strings.SPS_the_restoration_of_falangism_desc:
Iberia, of what use was such a union to Spain? Rather than uniting the peninsula under strong Spanish rule, Franco simply made new factions of government to frustrate the proper administration of our proud nation. Portugal's weaker revenues, frustrating policies, endless commitments; who could possibly defend such an arrangement with a nation so paralysed by itself?

The notion of Iberia is abolished; it never existed to begin with. This artificial creation to enrich the corrupt heart of Spain will finally be brought into proper light, and the People will reject the madness that it evidently was. Spain has found her heart again, reclaimed it from her abusers, and with this new heart a proud, independent Spain shall once more be heard.
strings.SPS_the_beginning_of_a_new_iberia_desc:
War required energy. There is nothing in this world that is not becoming something new, and war represents the primary proof of that. A new Spain is needed, one molded by the horror of our current peninsula to become all the stronger, to never forget the orgy of chaos by which we find ourselves beset by. Our children must never again experience such terror, all must be safeguarded from such a cruel fate as that which has been dealt to us.

The War must become a core foundational myth for ourselves, etched into the consciousness of all those who love Spain. This War must not become an uncomfortable memory to be sidelined, as too many did for the last one. The steel, the blood and the screams must never be washed from our hearts as we move into the future. Our future is united, our fate is unified, and only by strength can we avoid shared terror.
strings.SPS_in_the_souls_of_the_people_desc:
While much of the former Iberian Armed Forces has answered our call to defend our homeland, the morale and skill of our brave boys at the front is not enough if we want to reign over Spain when the war is over. The army is always hungry for new equipment and new men in order to expand, and, unfortunately, replace those who gave their lives for the cause.

In order to sustain the war effort, we absolutely must keep the home front on our side, or at least make sure that enough of the civilian population acquiesces to our rule. The people will see that we care for them, beyond the empty slogans of liberals and communists, and in turn, they will reward us with their support and their service.

Spare no expense when it comes to the battlefront, making sure that our enemies stand no chance against us. Only a swift and decisive victory will allow us to continue building a strong Spain.
strings.SPS_and_on_the_battlefields_desc:
While the home front is vital, the war will be won or lost on the frontline. We have under our control a large part of the former Federal Armed Forces, and with continued investment and support, we will cement our place as the strongest and most experienced military power on the peninsula.

However, as strong as we are, we must also be quick. Spain will be reforged in the fires of war, but we must not let those flames burn it for too long. A drawn-out campaign will leave the country devastated and our legitimacy contested. Spain must be able to stand on its own two feet and look forward to a unified destiny as soon as possible, and for that to happen, we must pursue a quick and decisive victory.

The “silent majority” that live in our territory does not pose a threat to our government but they certainly aren't enthusiastic about the war. We have to invest in convincing these people so that they will fully participate in the war effort.
strings.SPS_convincing_the_unconvinced_desc:
While plutocratic liberals and godless communists threaten us on the front and attempt to spread their venom from within, our greatest enemy is apathy. Most people who live in the territories we control do not pose a threat to our government, but they will not take up arms for our cause, either. That must change.

We will coordinate a campaign of propaganda and social policies targeted directly at this “silent majority.” If we are to win this war, it is not enough that they don't stand against us - we must convince them that we are the only hope for a strong, prosperous, and free Spain, and that this hope is bright enough for them to fully participate in making it into a reality.

Use any possible avenue to spread propaganda. Presses from banned newspapers will be given to friendly publications. Radios will be forced to increase the amount of “patriotic programming”. TV schedules will focus solely on our victories and what we will do once the war is over.
strings.SPS_spreading_the_good_word_desc:
In order to mobilize as much of our population as possible and make them willing participants in our great work, we must reach them. We will direct our propagandists to make sure that our message reaches every crowded apartment and every peasant household, and make use of all available means to help them in this endeavor.

Printing presses confiscated from traitorous newspapers will be given to more friendly publications. Radios will be directed to give more airtime to specially written, patriotic programming. Televisions will only show the people our great victories and the great future awaiting Spain once we have vanquished the Reds and the secessionists. Whatever it takes, the people will know who they should side with.

Create a temporary organization to aid police forces to root out possible dissidents and keep an eye over the population to make sure they work towards our victory.
strings.SPS_agencia_por_la_limpieza_social_desc:
While our propaganda department works night and day to bring our message and convince the people of our just cause, there must also be a stick to accompany the carrot. Dissidents and enemy agents still infest our territories, undermining our work among the civilian populace and weakening the morale of our boys on the front, and a strong hand is required to make sure they are rooted out as efficiently as possible.

To that end, we will set up the Agency for Social Purity - a temporary, wartime organization whose stated objective will be to aid our police forces in their hunt for traitorous and enemy elements in our rear. They will be granted significant powers of oversight over the population, punishing displays of unpatriotic behavior and making sure that all Spaniards contribute to our final victory.
strings.SPS_elevating_the_cause_desc:
This is not a petty conflict over simply earthly affairs, the very soul of Spain is at stake! With such dire stakes, it only makes sense that we must turn to those most learned in salvation to guide our people. We must turn to the Church.

The clergy shall become partners in our ministry, placing the true faith into its proper position in this war. From every pulpit, sermons shall condemn the degeneracy of the South. Every missal will ensure the People's proper commitment both to God and the State that supports him. From dusk till dawn we shall word for God, ever will we fight for him, and the Church will ensure all Spain knows it. Should any priests or Church organizations dissent from this undoubtedly holy duty?

Treason remains an earthly affair.
strings.SPS_the_foundations_of_a_state_desc:
While much focus is placed on the mind of a state, all too often its limbs rot forgotten beneath the weight. An effective civil service is essential to the efficient governance required to win this war, and yet so much of our apparatus fled south to indulge in their treachery. Such a state of affairs will not do.

Large recruitment drives shall be carried out, our net cast wide in order to find candidates of proper commitment, ability and morality to be the arms of the new Spanish State. With such a renaissance of morality in our administration, only the virtuous ideas of ours will permeate the apparatus. A golden age lies waiting.
strings.SPS_with_allies_amidst_the_union_desc:
Spain is cracked apart, that is a state of affairs few need reminding. However, not all cracks are immediately visible. There remain many power brokers yet uncommitted, factions that view the Republic with disdain but are yet to be entirely convinced of our efficacy. While such hesitation is frustrating, it is an obstacle that can certainly be overcome.

Directives shall be implemented with the intentions of improving our image. Public, selective displays of mercy. Operations to gain control of their influence networks. Outreach to their most agreeable figures. They shall come to love us, and with that love aid us in crushing the Republic before it can corrupt more of our precious nation.
strings.SPS_with_traitors_surrounding_us_desc:
We are not inhuman. It pains us to see the corruption infesting so many of our citizenry, however like an infected arm we would be unwise to allow sentimentality to permit further spread of the sepsis. From farm to street, traitors must be found and rooted out. Any official, politician or officer who has not demonstrated themselves as singularly loyal to great Spain must be removed. Public safety operations and propaganda will be stepped up, encouraging new waves of reports and arrests of any likely spies or infiltrators.

Only a clean Spain can win this fight. A Spain clean of the infestations of liberalism and socialism. A Spain pure in the hands of true believers.
strings.SPS_the_militias_take_hold_desc:
Spanish men at arms form a key part of the national pacification, true patriots rising to fight corruption where they see it without waiting for the rigidity of military organisation to direct them. Such enthusiasm should inspire us all, and in the early days of our conflict surely made a difference. However, to win the war rather than merely survive our first days, greater coordination must be achieved.

Rather than integrate militias directly and entrap ourselves within an organisational quagmire, we shall form a special place in our structure for such militias. While our core military shall meet the brunt of our enemy, the militia's both in our territory and the enemy's shall prepare the way. From policing to raiding, pressure shall be taken from our professional forces, freeing up crucial manpower and resources while ever sapping theirs, allowing our military to lead us to victory.
strings.SPS_a_page_from_the_civil_war: A Page from the Civil War
strings.SPS_a_page_from_the_civil_war_desc:
During the First Civil War, militias ran free across the countryside. They were used en masse, fielded in large numbers, and died en masse as they were thrown into frontline combat. Wise men that we undoubtedly are, we have learned from those days. The General Staff has conceived of a new way to use the militiamen.

Because most trained soldiers are required for frontline work, the militiamen should be used in place of them. Their new duties will include acting as garrisons, infiltrating enemy lines and doing damage, and scouting work. These jobs are more suited to irregular forces, as our commando program remains tiny and we have no other dedicated garrison troops or scouts.
strings.SPS_a_cohesive_fighting_force_desc:
The militias, while useful initially, have become a liability. They are too undisciplined to be properly controlled, and the moment when the decision was made to allow them to act independently, while useful for the circumstances it was originally conceived in, has passed.

 Our militias will be disbanded and heavy weapons returned to government control. To ensure a secure transition, officers in the militia who also had ranks in the Iberian Union military will receive that same rank in our new army.
strings.SPS_maintaining_the_frontline_desc:
As in all civil wars, ours has produced utter chaos. With the outbreak of open armed conflict, we were at least able to tell who our enemies are - those being the men wearing uniforms unlike our own. With that open armed conflict, however, there has come a new kind of chaos.

Strategic planning in our nascent state is constantly a challenge, due to the fluid nature of the lines, but it is crucial we maintain order and keep our frontlines fully-manned, for even a minute gap in the lines could be exploited by the enemy.
strings.SPS_a_spanish_war_economy_desc:
In these times, even the most optimistic of military planners recognizes that we need equipment. Speaking broadly, there are two sources for that equipment: domestic production and foreign shipments. The latter can be held up in blockade, stymied by embargo, etc. The former operates under no such restrictions, and at this juncture, quantity is more important than quality when it comes to military materiel.

It is for this reason that it is necessary to divert a large portion of the industry to produce weapons, trucks, planes, and all the necessary bits and bobs we need to save Spain from those who would besmirch her. If that means taking resources from civilian production to prioritize military industry, so be it; after all, we cannot stop the enemy's advances through hope and happy populations.
strings.SPS_making_use_of_international_aid_desc:
As the true leaders of Spain, we enjoy a wide variety of foreign networks ranging from supporting nations to sensible organizations. As heirs to the Union, our military and economy require all they can get, especially to outpace the usurpers. The eyes of the world have turned to our suffering homeland. It is essential that those eyes see the necessity of aiding our cause.

From overseas, crucial armaments and resources untouched by the chaos of our collapse can be sourced. Our soldiers will have access to high quality weapons with which to retake our homes. Our economy will have access to the resources required to supply the reclamation. The voice of Spain has called out, its harvest will help us march into the day.
strings.SPS_mobilize_the_industries_desc:
The core of a nation is their industry, the lifeblood of its people, and with the core of Spain divided so too is that lifeblood. Across the nation, usurpers and traitors have overtaken cities and towns where once the heart of our industry pumped. Spanish factories produce arms to fight Spanish patriots, from the large factories of the Republic to the small workshops of local terrorists.

But, all is far from lost. We were able to protect much of our industry during the collapse and it now stands ready to fuel the national pacification. In our secured territory rests the potential of numerous industrial complexes and small manufacturers waiting to be seized. Through legislation reorganizing the factories, through money to fund their owners and through campaigns to inspire their workers, every bit of manufacturing power we have will have one guiding purpose; liberation.
strings.SPS_the_question_of_logistics_desc:
Our nation is no doubt one of diverse challenges, and the chaos of civil strife merely accentuates this, especially when trying to consider how to keep the pacification efforts coordinated and supplied. The huge variety of terrains, levels of development, regional economies, local political leanings, resistance movements, militias, our own military - the list of complications imposes upon even the most determined planner. It's enough to make heads spin, and yet it is essential that we master them.

Supply routes nationally will be considered and laid out. All maps and intelligence we can get our hands on will be employed to create our networks, both for our territory and territory soon to be taken, so our soldiers will always know where their next meal and bullet can be found. The Homefront will be rationed and controlled if necessary; everything needed for the front shall make it there.
strings.SPS_the_old_guard_rises_strong_desc:
In recent years, the Union has regrettably shut down many men due to the vigor of their convictions. Particularly, the 'Blue' faction of the military and their loyalty to the ideals of the Falange earned them shunning from officers outside of their cliques. Iberia saw them as liabilities. However, now Spain needs men of such proud patriotism.

The Blue faction fully controls our military and will actively shape it around the ideals of fraternity and national freedom, to ensure the men who protect Spain carry its greatest beliefs with them wherever they go. Unified around a clear cause and common methodology, we shall avoid replicating the disjointed chaos of the other factions.
strings.SPS_pulling_from_the_unions_ranks_desc:
Not all of those who served Iberia have reenlisted with our forces. Many of these revealed themselves as traitors, fleeing to join the Republic. However, some have remained in our territory, refusing to betray us but evidently hesitant to join us as well. Further, many in government share those sentiments, looking upon these idle soldiers with distrust due to their questionable loyalty.

Despite the conflicts, now is the time for solidarity; we need men, skilled men. All can agree that the Republic risks the soul of Spain itself, and these men will be encouraged to reenlist upon that premise. They have demonstrated their loyalty to the nation and will surely fight with all their hearts for it. Should anyone's loyalty to the State flounder, then such individuals can easily be removed.
strings.SPS_a_pure_movement_desc:
We may commiserate with any soldier willing to shed their blood for our movement of restoring Spain, especially in such a perilous time. Then again, the spirit of the fighting bull can be harmed not just by obvious predators, but parasites that are just as mortally wounding. Officers in our enlistment could have their spirits falter by mere cowardice in times of need, and their tardiness to defend our territories would be more damning than a mere loss in a battle.

The remnants of our armed forces, no matter the size, must maintain its purity. Only known members of patriotic groups, such as the Falange or CT, may ever be promoted to higher command. Foot soldiers with no such hope for promotion can merely show no sign of perfidious behavior, as that is the most they can do.
strings.SPS_a_competent_high_command_desc:
Withstanding enemy forces bound to wreck our crumbling pillars of a new Spain may not be a pie-in-the-sky situation, but only with the rectification of the mode of command can this be achieved. Men may bicker and vacillate over whether High Command can put the spirit of Falange on a high pedestal, when the time wasted on diatribes could have helped turn the tide of the civil strife around, and the question of our ideology can be discussed in a more ideal time.

Officers who could demonstrate a dexterous level of command may find their chances of promotion improved, as even loyalists may not render their overzealous actions as officious. With our best leading our troops to succeed in their objectives, a blind eye can be turned on High Command for now.
strings.SPS_a_defensive_doctrine_desc:
The fighting spirit of the fine soldiers and loyal militia forms the greatest backbone of our military campaign, and it is crucial that we do not let it go to waste in a series of unnecessary and costly assaults. While we may not be able to overwhelm the rebels for now, we can still make use of the many opportunities that arise on the battlefield. Minimizing offensive operations and focusing on exploiting enemy mistakes can ensure that the fighting valor of the fine Iberian man will no longer be bled dry in quixotic assaults on fortified positions, securing a strong basis for decisive battles to follow.

Army officers must realize that prudence is not cowardice, and withholding forces in anticipation of future opportunities does not equal reticence. We shall instill a defensive doctrine that will punish the rebels' every mistake while minimizing our own losses.
strings.SPS_grinding_at_the_union_desc:
Favorable outcomes of the past campaign cycle meant that our forces now outnumber the rebels, and now it is time to exploit our advantage. We must not allow the enemy an opportunity to recuperate and reorganize their forces. Instead, our commanders will aggressively assault the enemy, making every passing day as costly as possible for the rebel war effort. This will help us maintain our numerical superiority while bleeding the rebels dry, to the point that they are powerless to stop our next offensive.

War is bloody business, and no battles are won without making heroic sacrifices in epic proportions. The attacks may not yield significant results and frontlines may stagnate, but ideology and zealotry will fortify our men and enable them to reach the final breakthrough. Our brave and loyal martyrs will sacrifice themselves and, in doing so, secure the final victory for our beloved Iberian state.

Army officers must be instructed to order assaults on enemy positions whenever troop morale and equipment stockpiles allow for such actions, provided that there exists a significant numerical superiority. Even when the frontline stagnates, repeated assaults will still be effective in depleting enemy stockpile, paving the road for easier victories in the future.
strings.SPS_breaking_the_stalemates_desc:
The rebel army is on the verge of rout, and all it takes is one last decisive operation to break its back. We must reinforce key battlefields where our troops have reached an impasse and use the fresh manpower to break through enemy lines. Exploiting our numerical advantage, we will embark on several such operations at once. The enemy will be powerless to stop us as we achieve the long-awaited breakthrough and allow our forces to advance quickly, bringing a decisive end to this drawn-out war.

These assaults will be pivotal for the future of Iberia. If we fail to achieve a breakthrough, all the accumulation and strategizing we conducted will be for nought. The choice lies with us – to seize the victory with a decisive breakthrough, or to let the conflict stagnate into a pointless bloodbath. The following days will decide it all.
strings.SPS_striking_down_from_the_skies_desc: If the rebels still cannot accept their fate, then let us rain hellfire from above. Our fighters will pave the way to secure control over the air, following which we shall ensure that every facet of their illegitimate regime is faced with the stark reality of the war. Our bombers shall strike not just their forces at the front, but also their important economic centers supplying guns and resources for their desperate last attempt to maintain a facade of resistance at the fronts. As the supply of guns and rations to the frontlines ceases, how long will rebel grit last?
strings.SPS_por_la_patria_el_pan_y_la_justicia: Por La Patria, El Pan Y La Justicia
strings.SPS_por_la_patria_el_pan_y_la_justicia_d:
From brimstone and gunsmoke rose the Spanish State as it defeated its corrupt predecessor, and from hellfire and ruins arises the Spanish State once more as it completes a National Revival to secure Spanish sovereignty in the Iberian Peninsula. Victory is within our grasp, and we shall grasp it with both hands as we establish a strong and free Iberia liberated from the malignant influence of corrupt foreign powers.

The rebels who denounce us seek only to return Spain to its weak and subjugated state prior to the Second World War. Their plan must not be allowed to reach fruition. In the vision of Caudillo Franco, we shall restore Spain to its prominent position on the global stage as a strong, prosperous, and, most importantly, independent power. None must be allowed to stand in our path. For Fatherland and Justice!
strings.SPS_wars.1.d:
Lieutenant Jorge paced anxiously around his cramped office in Toledo, frantically flipping through the pile of reports and folders he was holding. He was searching for something, anything, to solve the unfolding chaos within the broadly useless documents. As if in an echo of his frantic thoughts, his once-meticulous office was awash with abandoned papers, chattering officers, and noise. So much noise.

Jorge turned to see a young, nervous corporal attempting to maneuver in the chaos, defensively clutching a fresh pile of reports. He wasn't who Jorge would usually ask to see, but who knew where half his staff were. Beggars couldn't be choosers, and he needed this message sent. Jorge stormed through the crowd, much less gracefully than the corporal, and began barking at him.

'Corporal! Tell the bastards over at the Alcázar that we need them at Avenida de la Union! Reds have started barricading the avenue and shooting! If the pigs don't show up soon we'll have to destroy the whole neighborhood to dislodge them! Tell them they're letting the communists take the fucking city!' The corporal nodded anxiously, dashing away.

Jorge stopped for a moment to catch his breath. How did it all come to this? This was not supposed to be his job. He was supposed to be with his troops at the front line now, squashing rebellious Basques or Portuguese. This was Guardia Civil nonsense, but they were slovenly absent; a useless waste of money and ammunition.

How could the Caudillo let it get this bad? He had saved Spain once - but perhaps what other officers were whispering was true. Perhaps the Caudillo was getting old. The Guardia Civil's absence brought images of American support and Jewish money to Jorge's mind. A chilling thought ran down the Lieutenant's spine.
strings.SPS_wars.1.a: Was the Caudillo still fit to rule Spain?
strings.SPS_wars.2.d:
Colonel Alfonso buried his face in the frigate's railing, closing his eyes to the blazing sun and the flag flying above the hot metal deck. His soldiers were safe; but he had failed. Tangier was lost. They had lost.

As the ship sailed into the ocean, the steel railing's heat grew unbearable. Alfonso welcomed it. A small price to burn clean his failure. The pale faces, Joaquín and Pablo's terrified screams and the stampede towards the ship kept flashing in his mind, as well as a question: How?

An answer came to his mind. Tangier had been effectively abandoned by the Iberians for weeks now, only the port still being held by his skeleton crew. “Too strategic to abandon, hold until relieved”, his orders had said, as he'd been forced to abandon nearly every defensible position they had in the city. He had waited too long to ask for reinforcements from across the strait. By the time he had, it was already too late. His hesitation had brought ruin.

A merciful breeze crossed Alfonso's face, but the heat underneath him grew too harsh to bear. He opened his eyes and slowly stood up straight, feeling the eyes of his soldiers fixed on him - he could not tell whether in admiration, curiosity, or disgust. He leaned over the rail and emptied himself into the Atlantic Ocean, letting out a silent scream of loathing as vomit floated on the blue water.

Holding tight to the rail with one hand, Alfonso grabbed binoculars from one of the sailors with the other, searching for the increasingly distant port just in time to see the dark red Moroccan flag being raised over the Port Office. He watched the fluttering flag for a few minutes.

The Empire was gone, and they had gone with it.
strings.SPS_wars.2.b: In the port's waters, a lone Iberian flag was sinking.
strings.SPS_wars.3.d:
Lieutenant-General Jaime Milans del Bosch stood in his command tent, along with three other officers. His table was almost invisible under the piles of maps and notes, yet he seemed able to navigate the mess. His subordinates followed with their eyes as he traced a front line on the largest map before them.

'If we move our forces from Galicia in time, we could consolidate in western Cantabria and take the fight to the Basques. What do you think?'

One of the junior officers piped up. “Sir, doesn't that expose our western flank? Aren't we supposed to stay here and counterattack when possible?'

Milans del Bosch smirked. ”The Portuguese are traitors, but they're little more than a house of cards. The Basques' - Milans almost spat out the word - “are more dangerous. Their uprising caused all of this chaos in the first place, and is threatening the unity of Spain itself! Understood?'

Silence hung. 'Sir', another officer interjected. ”What about our positions here? What should we tell Madrid?'

Milans del Bosch pinched his nose for a moment and sighed, before looking up. “Lieutenant, what is this map?'

'A map of the Union, Sir'.

'Wrong.' Milans del Bosch picked up the map and tore it in half, clawing at the paper in the face of his shocked subordinates. ”The Union is gone. Weak men couldn't hold this land together, and the traitors have come out of hiding. The only government left is that which can assert itself. We have the opportunity to consolidate Spain and assert ourselves. Then, and only then, can we recover what's ours. That which belongs to Spain. Arriba España!'
strings.SPS_wars.3.a: That evening, Lieutenant-General Milans del Bosch's command began marching east.
strings.SPS_wars.4.d:
Antonio Barroso y Sánchez-Guerra was enraged. He slammed the door behind him with a grunt, and practically tossed a chair sitting askew to the sole table, slumping down onto it. In one hand, he held a report recounting events he had personally witnessed, personally agonised over, reduced to detached statistics. Taking a breath and peering into nothing, Sánchez-Guerra took a deep breath, mulling over what few revelations it could give him, hoping to steel himself for days ahead.

His unit had been assigned to Catalonia for some time, assigned to countering partisan activity. Even as funds and resources dried up, overstretched by vigorous activity nationwide, he nonetheless managed to retain a vague modicum of control over the province. Security was strong, and managed by high morale. Through the thick haze of disappearances, public trials and executions, he had managed to make a name for himself as relative peace was secured around Girona.

But then the Basque seceded, the weakness of a few regiments in the north condemning the Union. Suddenly, his regiment found itself facing renewed opposition, rapidly depleting as partisan activity rose alongside desertions, their names marked in deteriorating detail. To the backdrop of budding pressure, both within the province and against the supposed failures of his compatriots, they were forced to disperse across the country. His forces had been forced into Toledo. Far from their actual base, and close to Franco.

He set the report down one last time. He knew that he would return to Catalonia. Franco's mad quest to unify Iberia had been madness, but that would not sink him. A new leader had to be installed at some point, one willing to lead Spain back to its former glory. In his mind, he could see decorated men goose-stepping over the mangled corpses of Catalan separatists, through quiet, respectful streets.
strings.SPS_wars.4.a: And then, he considered an offensive aimed at cutting off Barcelona.
strings.SPS_wars.4.b: And so, he agonised over how they would defend against him.
strings.SPS_wars.5.d:
Lieutenant Oscar Cápitan lifted off his cap, wafting it toward his head as he watched the silhouettes of a few soldiers march beneath the tinted, setting sun. The past few weeks had been a blur, the past few days an utter nightmare. Past failures had emboldened separatists, and had only excited rioters. He refused to betray his emotions so openly, but struggled to stop his face turning to displeasure.

“Commandant Sandoval, sir,” spoke one, snappy and regimented as he halted in front of Cápitan. “You wanted to speak to us?”

Oscar's mouth tugged upwards, but only fleetingly. “Of course. I've received reports of rioters down in Asturias. No separatists there yet, but we both know it's only a matter of time.”

“Indeed, sir,” responded Álvaro, an echo in tone and disgust.

Oscar looked over his shoulders to watch over the others that had accompanied him. None seemed willing to refute their claim, but they looked at him with suspicion. “Police forces have been pooled in where they can be afforded, but it isn't enough. We're needed to boost numbers, and to ensure order is maintained.”

Another man refused to stay silent. “But sir, we can't just attack rioters,” responded Ferran Blázquez, a reservist drawn in at the last minute as Spanish forces had evacuated Catalonia..

“We could still negotiate with a few of the-”

“Did I not give you an order?” snapped Oscar, “You are a soldier loyal to Iberia, you do not question orders.” Ferran gave a brief apology, voice wavering, but the disobedience stuck in Oscar's mind as the small troupe marched out.
strings.SPS_wars.5.a: Perhaps the rot really was spreading downwards.
strings.SPS_wars.6.d:
Walking around the table, populated with emptied glasses and strewn papers, Tomás García Rebull found himself taken aback. He had expected fewer people to come; the remnants of the Iberian military was only ever getting more overstretched by the hour. However not one man had missed the meeting, placing a degree of welcome strain on Rebull himself.

“Well, Tomás, did you find that useful?” asked Manuel Valdés Larrañaga, still standing in the doorway and surprised at Rebull's slow pace as he turned around. “I definitely found some positions to be... fascinating, shall we say..”

“I think these officers have had enough, Manuel,” replied Rebull, moving towards Larrañaga. “This government has lost the confidence of everybody, even those in the military. Those loyal to Spain have grown tired.”

Larrañaga shrugged slightly, an attempt to save face. He had been worried by the decision, fearing it to be too visible a statement against Franco's authority, but had finally consented. “I agree. I really did expect better from Franco and had always set aside my concerns with the Union over his leadership. But who can justify some of his moves here? Seems some of the wider officer corps share the feeling.”

Rebull folded his arms as he raised an eyebrow. Shaking his head, he returned to a walking pace. “You underestimate. We can't squander this opportunity. This is the perfect time for us to strike. These officers are ready for Franco to leave, whether or not his body gives out first.”

Larrañaga sighed, filled with fatigue for the regime. “I'll move ahead with our plans, then. I'll contact Pérez-Viñeta and Codón, and will start to negotiate with a much wider section of the army first.”
strings.SPS_wars.6.a: “...I'm sure something else will crack for Franco first, though.”
strings.SPS_wars.7.d:
The room around Carlos Iniesta Cano was small, yet the lack of attendance helped to inflate its size. Franco had tried to call a meeting, ostensibly to coordinate those actively engaged in fighting, but Cano thought he could recognise attempts to secure preserved loyalty. As he visibly struggled to get comfortable at the head of the table, Cano briefly wondered if it was him expecting more generals to come.

“I'm glad that you were able to spare the time to meet, gentleman,” said Franco, his anger palpable. “Some within our midst think that they're too important, but I'm glad that not every bastard ignores their Caudillo. Any updates on strategy?” His voice was raspy, his face bitter, but the room still erupted into silenced shock. Cano looked ahead with suspicion.

“Well, we managed to suppress riots in León,” responded one of the few attendees, identified via name card as being Vergara, a junior officer who still seemed to be nervous. Definitely not the first call; Cano questioned if he was second. “We want to send forces to help those in Vigo.”

Franco looked at him for a second. Cano struggled to make out if he was even trying to speak as the Caudillo's eyes seemed to be tinted with mist. “That will be good. We need strong men to stop the León riots.” Another moment of silence extended itself, eyes looking around in bewilderment as Franco offered no further input.

The meeting continued, and then concluded. Cano watched in horror as the scene continued, listening as whispering officials with eyes of traitorous thoughts rushed out from the farce. Franco himself winced, struggling to limp away. His posture looked shrunken, his body limp and head wrinkled. Cano walked behind him, no longer wondering why so few members of the military wanted to be reminded of their leader.
strings.SPS_wars.7.a: Franco couldn't defend a village now, let alone a country.
strings.SPS_wars.8.d:
The topic of discussion within the heart of an impromptu military base in Valladolid had long since slipped away from its official pretence, but nobody paid it any heed. Rooms had been slapped together, with the jagged ruins of abandoned villages extended by white tarps thrown over wooden pikes on either end. Groups of Falangists and Carlists huddled together, distancing themselves as much as possible around tables, with gaps filled by some sceptical officers brooding with stolid dread.

“I have support from practically every man under my command, as well as many in Franco's cabinet,” said Carlos Iniesta Cano, bluntly. “It's not a decision I take lightly, but forming a junta now would stop the bleeding. The situation could be resolved in our favour within a few days should we apply pressure carefully.

José María Valiente clutched his hands tightly, bringing them closer towards him. ”We don't have many figures able to rally the country quite like Franco...“ he replied, monotonously. ”I have men in meetings with the Duke of Madrid right now. If we can afford to wait slightly longer, we could have him coronated.“ A few protests came from Falangists, mostly ignored by Valiente and actively hushed by the moderates among them.

Suddenly, a junior officer rushed in, carrying a radio in one arm sputtering poorly transmitted whispers blurring the line with static. ”Hello? Hel... is Colonel Ordóñez... Galicia is lost...“ snarled the one clear voice, silencing the meeting. ”Separatists have seized La Co... withdrawal from Orense... new republic headed by Xosé Velo...“

The meeting stewed in silence for a moment, stunned by the development. Finally, José María Valiente relented. ”I understand now. I thought we still had time, but we can afford a later coronation. Franco must go. A Junta needs to be proclaimed now.“
strings.SPS_wars.8.a: “Whilst there's still a Kingdom to be ruled.”
strings.SPS_wars.8.b: Flee from this madness to the mists of Galicia.
strings.SPS_wars.9.d:
The time for Franco to leave had long since passed, and yet he continued to linger. Despite that, Cano did not put much stock into the issue. His time as Caudillo was coming to an end, with significant efforts to motivate that end among the Iberian military. Even still, as he moved to phone Luis Carrero Blanco through the halls of a small, cramped bunker, he feared the potential response, and feared a last rally that could still sink them both yet.

“I don't have all day, Carlos.” said Blanco through the line in a hushed tone. “I've got enough on my plate even ignoring the latest developments.”

Cano sighed. “I've heard. A republic has been declared in Seville, and has been rapidly gaining support across the south.” An exaggeration, he thought, but only barely. “Franco will not be safe remaining in Madrid.”

Silence came down the phone line, one that could be ill afforded. “Maybe, but leaving wouldn't be wise, Carlos,” responded Blanco, audibly nervous yet still frustrated at the question. “By withdrawing so soon, we risk dissolving our support with most loyalists remaining in the country.”

The response came almost as a relief. These concerns were practically capitulation. “Their numbers are dwindling anyway,” spoke Cano, allowing himself to smile slightly. “Most officers I've been in contact with are actively pushing for a coup. I know a few regiments outside the city might still be loyal, but fifth columnists are teeming in Madrid.”

A groan came down the line, followed by a few muffled shouts, and then silence for another brief moment. “I will talk with Franco, but if what you say is true, then it might be wisest for us to leave after all, until loyalty is secured in the region.” Blanco continued with minutiae, demanding purges and names, pushing for a loyalty that Cano had long since lacked.
strings.SPS_wars.9.a: All of that melted away in Cano's mind, now awash with the next step.
strings.SPS_wars.10.d:
From the vantage point of a small tower, one of the few remaining relics of a small military base that had long since been scuttled, Carlos Iniesta Cano watched the commotion beneath him with arms clenched behind his back. A few small figures pushed carts into the gaping maw of a plane, whilst a few more escorted other small figures that he knew were Franco and his family. A handful more swept the area, looking for potential assassins, keeping watch elsewhere. Cano allowed Franco that luxury.

“Sir!” shouted an aide, breathless as he rushed forwards. “I've got reports from Valladolid.”

“I presume that this is about the coup?” Cano responded, grinning. With Franco leaving the city, and the country itself, he struggled to see any opposition remaining.

“Yes, it is.” Cano considered leaving the thought to linger for a moment, the notion of now being the most influential figure in the Junta simmering in his mind, but decided against it. “It was successful. A few isolated pockets tried to resist, but quickly surrendered and with minimal casualties on either side.”

Cano turned around to face the aide, mulling over the information. “I suppose there's some benefit to loyalty even when misguided. We should purge the most dangerous, but in these difficult times, we can't purge soldiers too freely.” He walked forwards slightly, stroking his chin as he considered any further vulnerabilities. “Any news on the front?”

The aide cringed slightly, but continued. “Nothing significant. The rebels and republicans have pushed slightly further, but are being held off.” No newfound pledges of loyalty; the issue seemed to have been worse than initially thought. But even still, thought Cano as he left to attend an imminent cabinet meeting in Valladolid, he had stopped the bleeding.
strings.SPS_wars.10.a: Franco's plane left the country, unnoticed by his successor.
strings.SPS_wars.12.d:
To all officers assigned to Zone 8 Block 3 in accordance with Emergency Directive 31.

Mr Juan Puebles, Floor 2 Room 23. Lives alone, veteran. Risk of firearms on premises.

Mr and Mrs Hugo López, Floor 2 Room 29. Mrs López, first name María, is suspected to be in an affair with a suspected communist. Bring both in. Mrs López should be capable of answering questions immediately so observe restraint.

Mr Javier Pérez, Floor 5 Room 50. Reported subversion tendencies. Family is to be left alone.

Mr Dario Sánchez, Floor 6 Room 62. Only son of resident Sánchez family, identified in underground student organization. High priority.

Mrs Marco Hernández. American born, first name Emily, 10 years residency. Possible involvement in socialist literature dispersal.

Mr Vidal Delgado, Floor 7, Room 70. Building proprietor. Due to the high number of suspected residents further interrogation required.

In all cases use of coercive force is authorized. Should local evidence suggest others at the address are possible suspects, under Clause 8 of the Emergency Directive officers are permitted to expand the number of detainees at the discretion of the nominated Zone Officer.
strings.SPS_wars.12.a: Options: With mathematical efficiency, the city shall be cleansed
strings.SPS_wars.13.d:
They stood in a line, blocking the path continuing down the Calle de Madrid. The street seemed claustrophobic to them all, the brick walls on both sides imposing down on them as they shared the red hue of the setting sun's sky.

The shouting could be heard before the mass could be seen.

The voices were young and light, demanding changes. A litany of banners and flags waved above the sea of student faces. Some flew red flags. Some flew black flags. Some flew the flag of the old republic, crudely made but unmistakable. Banners called for socialism. The end of martial law and dictatorship. Despite the diverse ideas they all chanted for one thing; liberty from the Francoists.

Many of the soldiers blocking them were of similar age, and shifted nervously. The command came to make ready, and they raised their rifles. An officer walked through a gap in the wall of soldiers, megaphone in hand, commanding the approaching column to disperse the illegal gathering. If not they would be fired upon - a threat met by jeering.

A lifetime passed and the crowd moved closer. The officer spoke again, some of the soldiers noting the masked pleading for the column to stop. The chanting instead called for the soldiers to break their chains and join them. Nervous eyes glanced at their comrades. Rifle barrels wavered.

The officer dropped the megaphone and put his head in his hands, walking behind the line of men. The column did not stop. 100 meters. 80 meters. 60 meters.

The order was given.
